## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `finished_at` column needs fixing before merge because it holds the `started` event's timestamp, so every running process shows a finish time. Its NULL documentation is also wrong for processes that were started and then cleared.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `finished_at` column to the `processes` current-state model and documents it in `models/schema.yml`. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` file.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Populate the timestamp from the right event, or rename it to started_at — For process 20, whose latest event is `started`, `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end as finished_at` gives a finish time of `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`, which is its start time. `sources/process_events.sql:4` allows only `created`, `started` and `cleared`, so no finish event exists. — Consumers of `processes` will treat every running process as finished at the moment it started. — Fix: Either rename the column to `started_at` and update `models/schema.yml:11`, or define which event marks a finish and use that event's timestamp.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Correct the NULL meaning for finished_at — For process 30, which was `started` and then `cleared`, the column is NULL, yet the documentation says "NULL means the process has never been started." The CASE expression returns a value only when the latest event is `started`. — Readers of the schema catalog will wrongly conclude that cleared processes never ran.
